scope: Worker implementation, focused Python regression, and independent read-only core integration review with a frozen two-scenario C++ nofollow harness. Full native/e2e/release acceptance remains parent-owned evidence.

findings.finding: Complete map page metadata is top-level http_cache; decoding only nested page omitted the validator base.
findings.resolution: Parent copies the top-level metadata into the page before decode_read and rejects disagreement when both copies are present.

findings.finding: Collecting the latest expired robots denial while older pinned rules remain could expose old validators after retention.
findings.resolution: Parent retains the newest decision until older rows can be removed, then collects the remaining singleton in a bounded additional pass.

findings.finding: Core rejected years before 1601 while Worker canonical date checking could accept earlier dates, turning a complete read into a protocol failure.
findings.resolution: Worker now uses the same lower year bound; 97 conditional tests passed, including two new old-date cases.

findings.finding: A failed refresh with nofollow but no noindex/nosnippet can change document_publication without a publication generation tracked by publication_history_locked; a later headerless 304 could recover snapshot follow_allowed and old links.
findings.requested_verification: Add failed-refresh nofollow -> headerless 304 -> crawl-frontier regression, and preserve the effective current follow restriction for 304 if confirmed.
findings.resolution: Core meets the effective current document policy in revalidation_base and ingest_web_locked; complete_map takes follow_allowed from the actual committed snapshot. Both restrictions observed before dispatch and during 304 processing remain effective.

evidence.worker_transport: in-process protocol fixture; this is not the real HTTP/Worker end-to-end test

code_reread: src/map.cpp: complete_map committed snapshot publication and E_NOFOLLOW edge

positive_checks: cached_robots selects the newest decision first and only then checks freshness; it does not skip a newer denial to admit old allowed content.
304 page commit checks owner/current snapshot/body/cache metadata identity and preserves the original body publication and site-generation boundaries.
Map 304 validates request/byte usage and robots decision, and rebuilds only retained, bounded complete discovery links.
Profile-only configuration changes remove conditions before the original GET; malformed bindings or unsupported 304 never trigger a retry.
Current document_publication is met with retained 304 policy both while preparing a base and again inside the ingest transaction.
Crawl expansion uses the committed snapshot publication.follow_allowed, so an in-flight nofollow observation blocks retained links.
The same frozen harness source, fixture and headers reproduced both nofollow cases with the old library and passed both cases after linking the fixed library.

independent_nofollow_validation.worker_transport: in-process protocol fixture; this is not the real HTTP/Worker end-to-end test

supported_subset_limits: Nonempty Vary and no-store/private/no-cache/max-age=0 metadata do not establish conditional bases in this protocol version.
Redirects strip conditions; unsolicited or invalid 304 responses fail without an additional network retry.
A request-profile-only change becomes the already-authorized original full GET, not an added request.
Crawl reuse requires an unchanged exact URL with no redirect and a complete retained discovery set of at most 512 links.
Only trustworthy retained robots rules with positive original freshness can be revalidated; an expired record alone cannot authorize content.
These local protocol fixtures do not claim acceptance of the default 17 external sources or full product release readiness.
followup: No outstanding issue in this delegated scope. Final release and external GitHub publication are parent-owned actions.
